findings.title: Cleanup logs informational messages at Error level and will flood logs with the new 1-minute ticker
findings.body: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579 in xorm_store.go use r.log.Error for purely informational messages about cleanup progress (e.g., 'Annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by time', 'Tags to clean', 'cleaned tags'). These are not errors and should be logged at Debug level. With the cleanup ticker now firing every minute (see cleanup.go:77), these messages will be emitted at Error level on every cleanup cycle, flooding logs and potentially triggering false alerts on log-based monitoring. Additionally, the 'err', err field at lines 534, 554, and 576 is always nil at that point (the error from fetchIDs was already checked and the function returned earlier if it was non-nil), which is misleading. The 'ids', ids field also logs every annotation ID at Error level, which for large cleanups produces very large log entries.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker frequency increased 10x (10 min -> 1 min) without justification in the PR description
findings.body: The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`, a 10x increase in cleanup frequency. This significantly increases database load (more frequent SELECT and DELETE queries against the annotation and annotation_tag tables on every Grafana node). The change is not mentioned in the PR description and does not appear necessary for the deadlock fix itself (which is achieved by splitting the subquery into separate SELECT and DELETE statements that don't share a transaction). No server lock is visible in cleanup.go to prevent concurrent cleanups across multiple Grafana instances, so this much higher frequency raises the risk of overlapping cleanups in clustered deployments. This is a notable behavioral change that should be called out in the release notes and ideally discussed separately from the deadlock fix.

findings.title: Cleanup loop terminates early when DELETE affects 0 rows, potentially leaving matching annotations uncleaned
findings.body: untilDoneOrCancelled terminates its loop when batchWork returns an affected count of 0. With the new split SELECT/DELETE approach, batchWork returns the affected count from deleteByIDs. If fetchIDs returns IDs but deleteByIDs affects 0 rows (e.g., because a concurrent cleanup process or another transaction deleted those same IDs between the SELECT and the DELETE), the cleanup loop exits without checking whether more matching annotations exist. The original code used a single atomic DELETE with a subquery, so 'affected == 0' reliably meant there were no more matching rows. The correct termination condition for the new split approach is len(ids) == 0 (no more IDs to fetch), not affected == 0. This regression can cause annotations to be missed in deployments where concurrent cleanups are possible. The fix is to either change the termination check to use len(ids), or have batchWork return int64(len(ids)) instead of the affected row count.
